message.content:
I'm selling one house on Illinois. Even-building rules make it the only property I can sell from right now. This raises $75 toward the $205 I'm short on the $800 rent to grok-4.7, leaving $130 still to cover.

After this sale all three reds will have 3 houses, so I can sell from any of them. Two more house sales would cover the debt and leave me about $20. I'm choosing to sell down rather than go bankrupt: my chances against grok-4.7 are slim, but staying in still gives me a chance.
message.reasoning:
I'm $205 short of the $800 owed, with $595 on hand. Houses sell for $75 each, but even-building rules mean only Illinois (with 4 houses, vs 3 for the others) can sell first—after that drops it to 3, all three properties are even and sellable. Selling 3 houses total covers the $225 needed, leaving $20 cash with houses down to 3 each.

Given p1's strong position with $818 cash and heavy development, my odds are slim, but staying in beats going bankrupt outright—so I'll proceed with selling one house at a time to work within the even-building constraint.
